# Plant database schema

The database is DuckDB.

## How queries run

The `run_sql` tool runs one query and returns its rows.

- Only SELECT queries run: a plain SELECT, a set operation of SELECTs (UNION, UNION ALL,
  INTERSECT, EXCEPT), or `WITH ... SELECT`. Every CTE must itself be a SELECT. Anything else
  is refused with a message: INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE, COPY, ATTACH, SET, INSTALL,
  PRAGMA, CALL, EXPLAIN, DESCRIBE, SHOW, VALUES on its own, and more than one statement.
  A comment after the final semicolon is fine.
- PIVOT and UNPIVOT work only inside a subquery: `SELECT * FROM (PIVOT ...)`.
- The database is read-only and the engine cannot read or write any other file. Use the
  tables below and table functions that generate data, such as `range`, only.
- A result may have at most 5,000 rows, and a query may run for at most 10 seconds. Past
  either limit the call fails with a message saying so. Aggregate in SQL rather than fetching
  raw readings.
- Functions and catalog views that show the engine's settings, files or internals are not
  available: any function or view whose name starts with `duckdb_`, `pragma_` or `pg_`, and
  `current_setting`, `which_secret`, `query`, `query_table` and
  `json_execute_serialized_sql`. The `information_schema` views work.
- The SQL dialect is DuckDB's. Engine errors are returned with the engine's message.

content.thinking: I need the energy per unit for each line in June 2026, so I'll first check the dataset's date range and use local time. Energy will come from summing line meter kWh over June local dates, and units from orders in June, with the attribution question still open, so I'll check that quickly while combining the queries.

input.sql: SELECT (SELECT timezone||' '||first_date||' '||end_date FROM dataset_info) info, line_id, count(*), min(start_utc), max(end_utc), sum(units), sum(CASE WHEN start_utc<'2026-07-01' AND end_utc>'2026-07-01' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) straddle_end, sum(CASE WHEN start_utc<'2026-06-01' AND end_utc>'2026-06-01' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) straddle_start FROM production_order WHERE end_utc>='2026-05-31' AND start_utc<'2026-07-02' GROUP BY line_id ORDER BY line_id

content.thinking: I'm working out the June window in local time, which is 2026-05-31 22:00 to 2026-06-30 22:00 UTC. Orders will be bucketed by their local start time in June, and energy readings by local date in June. I'll check whether the line meters have readings and fall back to summing the machines when they don't.

input.sql:
WITH e AS (SELECT meter_id, sum(kwh) kwh, count(*) n FROM reading WHERE local_date BETWEEN '2026-06-01' AND '2026-06-30' GROUP BY meter_id),
m AS (SELECT p.meter_id line, sum(e.kwh) kwh FROM meter p JOIN e ON e.meter_id=p.meter_id WHERE p.level='machine' GROUP BY 1),
u AS (SELECT line_id, sum(units) units FROM production_order WHERE timezone('Europe/Rome', timezone('UTC', start_utc))::date BETWEEN '2026-06-01' AND '2026-06-30' GROUP BY 1)
SELECT l.meter_id, e.kwh / NULLIF(u.units,0) AS value, e.kwh, e.n, (SELECT sum(e2.kwh) FROM meter mm JOIN e e2 ON e2.meter_id=mm.meter_id WHERE mm.parent_id=l.meter_id) mach_kwh, u.units
FROM meter l LEFT JOIN e ON e.meter_id=l.meter_id LEFT JOIN u ON u.line_id=l.meter_id WHERE l.level='line' ORDER BY 1

content.text:
Here is the energy used per unit produced (kWh/unit) on each of the 10 production lines for June 2026:

| meter_id | value (kWh/unit) |
|---|---|
| line_a1 | 12.83 |
| line_a2 | 8.52 |
| line_a3 | 8.72 |
| line_b1 | 7.53 |
| line_b2 | 4.30 |
| line_b3 | 3.56 |
| line_c1 | 9.64 |
| line_c2 | 11.85 |
| line_d1 | 2.10 |
| line_d2 | 1.44 |

Stamping line 1 (line_a1) used the most energy per unit and Assembly line 2 (line_d2) the least. Every line had a full month of readings, so none of the values are missing.

How I worked it out:
- **Month boundaries:** June means June 1–30 in the plant's local time zone (Europe/Rome), not UTC.
- **Energy:** I used each line's own meter, not the total of its machines. The line meter reads about 3–7% higher than the machines combined, so it includes some line-level load the machines don't show. If your review counts machines only, the figures would be that much lower.
- **Units:** I counted the units from every order that started in June in local time and gave each order to the month it started in. A few orders that started in late June finished in early July, and one or two at the start of June began very early in the morning. Counting orders by end date, or splitting them across months, would shift the figures a little.
